## WorkOS Magic Link Email Delays

Emails might be delayed when Enhanced Pre-delivery Message Scanning is enabled on a Google workspace or when a similar feature is enabled with other email providers.

## General Email Delivery Factors

If issues exist for all users, it's most likely a matter of poor domain reputation. If the issue only exists for a subset of users, it may be because of specific settings used by an email provider or the IT department at a given organization.

## WorkOS Recommendations

WorkOS follows industry best practices when sending email, with SPF and DKIM email authentication records configured automatically, email content continually refined to ensure it passes spam filters, and delivery of every email actively monitored.

## Known Issues with Magic Links

It's worth noting that Magic Link is not recommended due to issues with email clients or other security software visiting the links and invalidating them. Instead, use Magic Auth, which provides a more secure passwordless authentication method.

If you're experiencing specific delays with WorkOS magic link emails in 2026, the documentation suggests checking your domain reputation and email provider settings, or contacting WorkOS support directly for assistance.

content.text:
No current WorkOS outages. The last incident was March 17 (elevated API errors, resolved within ~90 minutes). Service has been stable since.

For slow magic link emails specifically, the most common causes are:

- **Enhanced Pre-delivery Message Scanning** on Google Workspace (or similar features on other providers) — this adds delay before the email appears in the inbox
- **Email provider spam filtering** — the magic link email might be landing in spam/junk
- **Domain reputation** — if it's slow for everyone, could be a reputation issue with the sending domain

WorkOS also notes that **Magic Link is deprecated in favor of Magic Auth** (which uses a code instead of a link), partly because email clients/security software can pre-visit links and invalidate them.

Could be worth asking affected users to check their spam folder, and whether they're on Google Workspace with scanning enabled.

Sources:
- [WorkOS Status](https://status.workos.com/)
- [WorkOS Email Delivery Docs](https://workos.com/docs/email)
- [WorkOS Magic Auth Docs](https://workos.com/docs/authkit/magic-auth)

message.content: Right I meant magic auth, not magic link. So is there anything I can do about this?

content.text:
The main levers are:

1. **Custom email domain** — Instead of emails coming from WorkOS's domain, you send from your own. This avoids shared reputation issues and looks more trustworthy to email providers. WorkOS docs cover how to set this up.

2. **Tell users to check spam/junk** — Especially first-time users whose provider hasn't seen the sender before.

3. **Google Workspace scanning** — If most affected users are on Google Workspace, that pre-delivery scanning delay is likely the culprit, and there's not much you can do on your end about it.

content.content:
# Custom Email Domain Setup

Based on the provided documentation, here's what's required:

## DNS Records Needed

To configure your own email domain with WorkOS, you need to set up **three CNAME records**:

1. One to "verify ownership of the domain"
2. Two additional records to "automatically configure SPF and DKIM email authentication using SendGrid's automated security feature"

The documentation also recommends setting up a **DMARC DNS TXT record** for additional authentication protection.

## Additional Setup Steps

- Create inboxes for both `welcome@<your domain>` and `access@<your domain>` addresses
- Configure DMARC with your domain provider (required by Google, Apple, and Yahoo guidelines)

## Plan Availability & Domain Provider Details

The documentation does **not specify** whether custom email domains are available on free plans, nor does it mention Vercel or provide domain provider-specific integration details.

For complete configuration instructions and plan eligibility, you would need to consult the WorkOS dashboard or contact their support team, as those details aren't covered in this content.

Based on the search results, here's what I found about WorkOS custom email domain pricing and free plan requirements in 2026:

## Custom Email Domain Pricing

Using custom domains with CNAMEs for AuthKit, the Admin Portal, and transactional emails incurs a flat fee of $99 per month. Using the default WorkOS domains is free.

## Free Plan Details

WorkOS User Management is free for up to 1 million monthly active users. Custom branding and custom domains can be applied for an additional monthly fee.

The key point is that while the base User Management product is free at 1M MAUs, **custom email domains are not included in the free plan** — they require a separate $99/month charge. This means if you want to use a custom email domain from your free plan, you'll need to pay this additional monthly fee.
